classification.difficultyReason: Choose intervals sharing a point, compare their gradients to identify a collinear triple, and distinguish the remaining point from that line.

content.prompt: Consider the points $A(-7,-11)$, $B(-4,-6)$, $C(-1,1)$ and $D(2,7)$. Only three of these points lie on the same line. Determine which three points lie on the same line.

answer.short: $A$, $C$ and $D$ lie on the same line.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}m_{AC}&=\frac{1-(-11)}{-1-(-7)}\\m_{AC}&=\frac{12}{6}\\m_{AC}&=2\\m_{AD}&=\frac{7-(-11)}{2-(-7)}\\m_{AD}&=\frac{18}{9}\\m_{AD}&=2\end{align*}$$
The intervals $AC$ and $AD$ have the same gradient and share $A$, so $A$, $C$ and $D$ are collinear. Also, $m_{AB}=\frac{-6-(-11)}{-4-(-7)}=\frac53\ne2$, so $B$ is not on this line.
